Darth Plagueis — Legends feat and statement extraction
Final URL: https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Darth_Plagueis/Legends
Scope: article body through Notes and references; navigation, trivia, appearances, and source lists omitted.

[FEAT/CLAIM] [Prelude] Several years before Hego Damask's birth, his father, a Force-sensitive Muun named Caar Damask, who worked as a middle-ranking Banking Clan agent, met renowned starship designer Rugess Nome—or Darth Tenebrous—by chance on High Port Space Center.[1] Tenebrous, in his capacity as reigning Dark Lord of the Sith, had been searching for the right apprentice to train for the sole purpose of eventually possessing through the virulent midi-chlorians he had dubbed "maxi-chlorians" in order for his consciousness to survive until the creation of the Chosen One, who would be seized by the Sith.[4]
  Source: Darth Plagueis ; "The Tenebrous Way" — Star Wars Insider 130 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1,4; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
[STATEMENT/HYPE — not a feat] [Prelude] Years after his meeting with Damask, Tenebrous discovered another Force-sensitive Muun—a lower-caste female—and conscripted her as a disciple, for she was not strong enough in the Force to be considered for apprenticeship.
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Prelude] Tenebrous, using Bith scientific methods, had predicted that the offspring of Damask and his disciple would be strong in the Force.
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Birth and early life] Before his fifth birthday, Hego discovered that he could manipulate the Force by using it to ply the feelings of his playmates.
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Birth and early life] He eventually tested the limits of this power by using a very potent mind trick on a Muun youngling he had grown to dislike, convincing the boy to commit suicide by jumping into a courtyard from a high window.
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Birth and early life] Damask's mother instructed her son to keep his powers secret, and confided in him that they shared the gift.[1]
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Birth and early life] Tenebrous took the child as his apprentice,[1] the one he intended to eventually possess,[4] naming him—at some unknown point—Darth Plagueis.
  Source: Darth Plagueis ; "The Tenebrous Way" — Star Wars Insider 130 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1,4; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Birth and early life] Plagueis left Mygeeto for the first time in his life, and began his life as a Sith.[1]
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Birth and early life] Five years after handing his son to the Dark Lord, Caar Damask was appointed director of the treasury branch of the InterGalactic Banking Clan, realizing his lifelong dream of wielding real power within the IBC.
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match]
[STATEMENT/HYPE — not a feat] [Darth Tenebrous and Darth Plagueis] But the Force works through us all the more powerfully in our invisibility."
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Darth Tenebrous and Darth Plagueis] During his travels, Plagueis became acquainted with the backwater of the galaxy; in the years to come, he would feel at home in the run-down spaceports, seedy tapcafs and rough cantinas common in the Rim.[1] Around the year 104 BBY, Plagueis undertook the trial of visiting Kursid and fighting its natives with Darth Tenebrous for the first time.[1]
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Darth Tenebrous and Darth Plagueis] Plagueis later told his own apprentice that his first mission under the tutelage of Lord Tenebrous was undertaken in the twenty-fifth year of his apprenticeship, at some point after 99 BBY:[5] Tenebrous tasked his apprentice to murder Kerred Santhe the Elder.
  Source: Mission to Lianna: "Less than one century ago, the planet was turned over to the control of Sienar Technologies, one of the most powerful and wealthy starship … ; Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 5,1; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Darth Tenebrous and Darth Plagueis] The assassination was accomplished by means of telekinetic strangulation during a banquet on Corulag; the Sith Lords took advantage of the fact that bloat eel was served in order to blame Santhe's death on the chefs.
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Darth Tenebrous and Darth Plagueis] Following this trial, Plagueis veered from the Sith path, as often happened with apprentices when they first discovered the potency of the dark side.[1]
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
[STATEMENT/HYPE — not a feat] [Darth Tenebrous and Darth Plagueis] Plagueis later claimed to Palpatine that he had returned to Muunilinst to meet the rest of his clan.
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Darth Tenebrous and Darth Plagueis] Soon afterwards, Caar Damask fell gravely ill at a relatively young age for a Muun, and it was discovered that he had a rare congenital defect in his tertiary heart that he had passed on to his children with his first wife.
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match]
[STATEMENT/HYPE — not a feat] [Darth Tenebrous and Darth Plagueis] Plagueis claimed that he had hired the geneticist to conduct phony treatments, and that he took pleasure in his siblings' early deaths, inheriting the wealth they had tried to deny him.
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Darth Tenebrous and Darth Plagueis] Palpatine suspected that the story was embellished to goad him into killing his family.
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Darth Tenebrous and Darth Plagueis] Instead, he sent him on various missions he judged pointless as a distraction, and cultivated his apprentice's unprecedented talent for midi-chlorian manipulation, all the while making sure that the Muun would only apply it to the preservation and extension of his own life, thus ensuring that he would live long enough for Tenebrous to possess the body of the Chosen One.
  Source: "The Tenebrous Way" — Star Wars Insider 130 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 4; exact text match]
[STATEMENT/HYPE — not a feat] [Darth Tenebrous and Darth Plagueis] Plagueis developed his powers in the Force and in the mundane world largely on his own, and indeed took them further than his Master believed.[4] Tenebrous also took on a second apprentice, a Bith to whom he bestowed the name "Darth Venamis." Although Venamis was apprised of Plagueis's existence, Plagueis was kept in the dark—he believed he was his master's sole apprentice, in accordance with the Rule of Two, a rule he had come to resent.[1]
  Source: "The Tenebrous Way" — Star Wars Insider 130 ; Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 4,1; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Darth Plagueis becomes the Master] 67 years before the Battle of Yavin, Darth Tenebrous learned of a cortosis deposit on the planet Bal'demnic, and personally went there to survey it with his apprentice, a treddroid, and an M-2 mining probe provided by Subtext Mining.
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Darth Plagueis becomes the Master] The enterprise soon came to an unexpected end, however, when the droid reported that the mining probe had discovered a pocket of a highly combustible variant of lethane directly beneath the borehole.
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Darth Plagueis becomes the Master] Tenebrous ordered the droid to have the probe deactivated, but it failed; the probe overrode the droid's commands.

[FEAT/CLAIM] [Darth Plagueis becomes the Master] After the two Sith unsuccessfully tried to damage the probe using Force lightning, they hastened to return to the grotto where they had landed the ship, leaving the treddroid behind.

[FEAT/CLAIM] [Darth Plagueis becomes the Master] It was then that Plagueis had the impression of hearing the Force whisper to him that his moment had come to claim his stake to the dark side, and lost no time in contemplation—he betrayed his master by bringing the huge slabs of stone down on him using the Force.
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match]

[FEAT/CLAIM] [Darth Plagueis becomes the Master] As Plagueis reached out in the Force to study Tenebrous's dying midi-chlorians, the maxi-chlorians carrying the Bith's intelligence slipped out of his body undetected and infected a wound on the Muun's lower back, caused by a rock or some other projectile.
  Source: "The Tenebrous Way" — Star Wars Insider 130 [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 4; exact text match]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Darth Plagueis becomes the Master] As the maxi-chlorian virus propagated inside Plagueis's cells, Tenebrous accessed his apprentice's powers of foresight, the powers he had had to give up himself in order to code his intelligence into the retrovirus.

[FEAT/CLAIM] [Darth Plagueis becomes the Master] What he witnessed horrified him: instead of providing access to the Chosen One, Darth Plagueis died at the hands of his own apprentice, "the shadow." After the retrovirus completed the task it had been engineered for, the infection of all the cells in Plagueis's body, the Muun Dark Lord lost his powers of foresight.

[STATEMENT/HYPE — not a feat] [Personality and traits] Darth Plagueis was considered a mystic,[16] despite the fact that he sought to develop an entirely rationalistic system of Force study, was among the few Sith Lords to have serious doubts about the existence of Force ghosts—even after confronting the purported ghost of Marka Ragnos—and was similarly weary of supposed prophecies.[8] That said, he believed in the signs and portents.[1] Plagueis was a devotee of the dark side, and a lover of things otherworldly and arcane.[21] Obsessed with the prospect of eternal life[16] and ideas of spontaneous generation,[22] he remained focused on matters of the material world,[21] though in later years Darth Vader mused that Plagueis had also desired a way to preserve the immaterial self after the death of the body.[18] Although Plagueis, as a Sith Lord, rejected common morality and interpersonal ties as artificial restrictions fabricated by the weak to control the strong, he did develop a genuine bond with his apprentice, Darth Sidious, in an attempt to break the cycle of death started by Bane and thus further their own goals.
  Source: The New Essential Chronology ; Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side ; Darth Plagueis ; Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide ; Vader: The Ultimate Guide ; Death Star [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 16,8,1,21,22,18; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
[FEAT/CLAIM] [Personality and traits] Plagueis's effort was not reciprocated, however, and Sidious ultimately betrayed and murdered his Master in cold blood.[1]
  Source: Darth Plagueis [per Wookieepedia "Darth Plagueis/Legends" rev 15697098, ref 1; exact text match; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
[STATEMENT/HYPE — not a feat] [Personality and traits] Plagueis was a vegetarian (though when direly hungry ate bats and even considered consuming people and took a bit out of a Kursid’s heart as a sign of dominance and savagery),[1] and possessed a logical mind,[23] and his apprentice Sidious believed that the extent to which he turned his sight inward was the source of his power and knowledge.[24] He also was able to think wisely and make sure to cover his tracks and also had a grim sense of humor.[1] When he wrote his journals on the nature of the Force, he wrote them primarily in Basic, although, in a chart he drew which demonstrated a triangular relationship between the aperion, anima, and pneuma, he curiously wrote his words backwards, with backwards Aurebesh characters.[8] He believed that power was to be gained incrementally, beginning with the self and culminating with control of the entire galaxy.[9] As his own powers grew, he became afraid of nothing but losing that power.[3] Plagueis was pathologically afraid of death, and this was the main reason he was chosen by Darth Tenebrous as an apprentice, Tenebrous would provide him immortality while Plagueis provided Tenebrous access to the Chosen One—or so Tenebrous thought—.[4] The Sith was willing to barter and bargain for passage with the Woebegone crew and honesty was confused by the idea of a ship having communal leadership.
